Subject: Request for processor chain + key escrow policy for EU pilot

Hi Chloe,

We’re kicking off a small EU pilot for a customer-facing feature on Nov 27 and need to complete our procurement/security checks this week. Please can you provide: 

- A full roster of subprocessors involved in request handling, telemetry, caching, and metrics for the EU region (including country of processing and export paths).
- A short diagram or description of how Redwood manages encryption keys for hosted and private deployments in the EU (HSM/KMS provider, whether keys are ever escrowed/exported, and who holds HSM access).
- Any relevant DPA amendments or redline templates we need to sign for the pilot.

We need to validate that no customer PII is routed outside the EU without suitable safeguards. If you can share a redacted subprocessor CSV and your KMS diagram today that would be ideal. If necessary, we can schedule a 20-minute call to clarify technical details.

Also include any SOC2 or audit evidence pointers related to key management.

Thanks,
Laura

Subject: Re: Request for processor chain + key escrow policy for EU pilot — technical details and artifacts

Laura / Chloe — attaching the technical artifacts requested. See brief answers below and the attached files (subprocessor_roster_20281114.csv, kms_diagram_v2.pdf, dpa_amendment_acme_v1.docx).

1) Key management summary (hosted vs private):
- Hosted (Redwood API): by default we use Redwood-managed keys in Azure Key Vault (eu-central) with HSM-protected keys; Redwood employees do not have plaintext key export capability.
- Dedicated/Private: customers may bring their own keys (BYOK) via a supported KMS provider (Azure, AWS, or on-prem HSM). In BYOK mode the customer retains key control; Redwood stores only wrapped keys and cannot decrypt without KMS authorization.
- Escrow: we do not maintain an escrow of customer keys for hosted customers. Escrowed keys are only used in highly controlled exit plans (on-prem migrations) with explicit customer sign-off.

2) Subprocessors & data paths: the attached CSV lists each processor role, country, and whether it sees payloads or telemetry. Note: caching and CDN layers in some EU countries are subcontracted; we mark these rows as telemetry-only where applicable.

3) SOC2/audit references: our key management controls are covered under CC-Crypto section; we can provide the specific SOC2 control IDs on request or provide a SOC2 summary package via a secure link.

4) DPA amendment: attached is a proposed amendment that covers the pilot scope and temporary telemetry access. Please route redlines to kimberly_park@redwood.com.

If you’d like, we can redact further fields in the CSV for any entries that would reveal customer-specific routing.

Regards,
Ben Carter
Security & Compliance — Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com

Attachments: subprocessor_roster_20281114.csv, kms_diagram_v2.pdf, dpa_amendment_acme_v1.docx
